Here is the complete project pitch and documentation in Markdown format. You can copy and paste this directly into a README.md or a Notion page to share with other developers or use as your master blueprint.
🕸️ Project AgentWeave (The Python ↔ WebMCP Bridge)
TL;DR: WebMCP is revolutionizing how AI agents interact with the web, but it only speaks JavaScript. AgentWeave is an open-source bridge that lets developers write powerful AI tools in Python (using FastMCP) and instantly inject them directly into any live browser tab. It’s the "Brain" of Python connected to the "Hands" of the browser.
📖 1. Introduction: The Dawn of the "Agentic Web"
Right now, if an AI agent wants to buy you a pair of headphones on Amazon, it has to download the page, read thousands of lines of messy HTML, guess which button says "Add to Cart," and simulate a mouse click. If Amazon changes a CSS class tomorrow, the agent breaks. It's clunky, slow, and brittle.
Enter WebMCP (Google's new standard):
WebMCP completely flips the script. Instead of agents guessing where buttons are, websites can use a new browser API (navigator.modelContext) to explicitly register tools.
When an agent visits the site, the browser hands it a clean menu: "Here is the search_products tool, and here is the add_to_cart tool." Even better, because this runs inside the browser tab, the agent automatically uses the user's active login session and cookies. No more messy API keys or OAuth setups!
🚧 2. The Problem: The "Adoption & Language" Gap
WebMCP is incredible, but it has two massive roadblocks right now:
The Adoption Problem: Giant sites like Amazon, eBay, or Shopify won't update their codebases to support WebMCP overnight. We are going to be waiting years for universal adoption.
The Language Barrier: WebMCP is 100% JavaScript (Frontend). But the AI revolution—including the powerful FastMCP servers, data cleaners, and LLM orchestrators—is built on Python.
There is a huge disconnect between the frontend web (where the user's session lives) and the backend (where the AI logic lives).
💡 3. The Big Idea: Project AgentWeave
AgentWeave is an open-source framework that acts like "Greasemonkey for AI Agents."
It allows you to inject WebMCP tools into any existing website, while keeping all the heavy-lifting logic in Python. We split the architecture into two simple parts:
The Hands (JavaScript Extension): A lightweight Chrome Extension that visits a site (like Amazon) and uses navigator.modelContext to announce new tools to any AI looking at the page.
The Brain (Python FastMCP Server): A local Python server running on the user's machine that actually executes the tool's logic, processes the data, and talks to the LLMs.
They talk to each other instantly via WebSockets.
⚙️ 4. How It Works (The Architecture)
Imagine a user tells their AI: "Find me a black IEM under 2000 rs on Amazon."
The Extension Injects: The user opens Amazon. The AgentWeave Chrome Extension detects the site and injects a search_products tool into the browser's WebMCP registry.
The Agent Acts: The AI agent sees this clean tool and calls search_products(query="IEM", color="Black", maxPrice=2000).
The Bridge Fires: The JS extension catches this call and instantly forwards the data over a WebSocket to your local Python server.
Python Does the Heavy Lifting: Your Python script (using tools like BeautifulSoup, Pandas, or an LLM) does the complex data scraping/cleaning of the Amazon page.
The Handoff: Python sends a clean, formatted JSON array back through the WebSocket to the browser, which hands it back to the Agent.
🚀 5. Why This is a Game Changer (Advancements)
Zero Wait Time for WebMCP: We don't have to wait for websites to adopt the standard. We can retroactively make the entire internet "Agent-Ready" today.
Empowering Python Devs: Python developers can now build browser-native tools without having to become React/JS frontend experts.
Community-Driven: Because it's open-source, the community can create a shared repository of "Site Configurations" (e.g., "Here is the AgentWeave config to make Netflix controllable by AI").
📅 6. Project Roadmap & Timelines
Phase 1: The Proof of Concept (Weeks 1-2)
Goal: Get a local Python script talking to a single browser tab.
Tasks:
Build a simple Python WebSocket server (bridge_server.py) that returns dummy data.
Write a vanilla JavaScript snippet (bridge_injector.js) that connects to the socket and registers a navigator.modelContext tool.
Test it manually by pasting the JS into the Chrome Console on a live site.
Phase 2: The "FastMCP" Integration (Weeks 3-4)
Goal: Make it seamlessly work with existing Python FastMCP code.
Tasks:
Build the pywebmcp Python package.
Create a wrapper so developers can just use a simple decorator (e.g., @agentweave.tool()) in their Python code, and the library auto-generates the WebSocket logic and input schemas.
Phase 3: The Chrome Extension (Month 2)
Goal: Automate the JS injection so users don't have to use the developer console.
Tasks:
Build a manifest V3 Chrome Extension.
Add a background script to manage the WebSocket connection to the local Python server.
Add a UI panel showing the user exactly which AI tools are currently active on the page (for security and transparency).
Phase 4: The Open Source Launch & Community Registry (Month 3)
Goal: Scale the project.
Tasks:
Clean up documentation and publish the Python package to PyPI.
Launch the Chrome Extension on the Web Store.
Open a GitHub repo called AgentWeave-Recipes where people can submit their custom Python-to-Web tool mappings for popular sites.
🤝 7. Next Steps to Start
To kick this off, all we need is a fresh IDE window.
Open Google Chrome Canary or Chrome 146+.
Enable the WebMCP flags in chrome://flags.
Boot up a Python virtual environment and pip install websockets fastmcp.
Let's weave the web!

Outgoing call to connect two numbers
Voice v1 APIs work without any user (call centre agent) context, i.e. they don’t need a user to be added to the Exotel dashboard and therefore don’t check a user number for busy status before calling that number.

This API will connect two numbers. It connects From Number first. Once the person at the From end picks up the phone, it will connect to the number provided as To. You can choose which number should be connected first by adding that number in the From field. An HTTP POST request is made to

POST
https://<your_api_key>:<your_api_token><subdomain>/v1/Accounts/<your_sid>/Calls/connectCopy
Try it
If you’d prefer response in JSON format, just append .json at the end of the HTTP POST request.

Replace <your_api_key> and <your_api_token> with the API key and token created by you.

Replace <your_sid> with your “Account sid”
Replace <subdomain> with the region of your account
<subdomain> of Singapore cluster is @api.exotel.com
<subdomain> of Mumbai cluster is @api.in.exotel.com
<your_api_key> , <your_api_token> and <your_sid> are available in the API settings page of your Exotel Dashboard

The following are the POST parameters sent as form-data in the Body of the Request:

Parameter Name Mandatory / Optional Value
From Mandatory String; The phone number that will be called first. Preferably in E.164 format. If not set, our system will try to match it with a country and make a call. If landline number, prefix it with STD code; Ex: 080XXXX2400
To Mandatory String; Your customer's phone number. If landline number, prefix it with STD code; Ex: 080XXXX2400
CallerId Mandatory String; This is your ExoPhone/Exotel Virtual Number (pick one from here)
CallType Optional String; trans - for Transactional Calls
TimeLimit Optional Integer; The time limit (in seconds) that you want this call to last. The call will be cut after this time (max. 14400 i.e. 4 hours)
TimeOut Optional Integer; The time (in seconds) to ring the called parties (both first and second call leg)
WaitUrl Optional 
String; Play this audio to the caller. When the first leg (From) has to wait for the other leg (To) to pick up the call, the audio file specified in this parameter will be played.

Please refer this article to understand the format specifications of the audio file to be played (wav is only supported).

Guidelines on usage:

The audio file size is recommended to be less than 2MB. Please note, Exotel will cache the wav file. During the first few call attempts of setting this parameter, user might hear normal ringing tone for first 5 seconds (for a ~2MB file). This is only temporary for initial few calls and once the audio file is cached, audio will be played out smoothly.
In case you decide to change the audio file later, the WaitUrl should be different (as Exotel will cache audio file based on URL). You can do so by hosting the audio file with a different name.
When using this parameter, it is recommended to set the TimeOut parameter as well.
Example: "http://{your_hosted_endpoint}/{audio file name}.wav"

Record Optional 
Boolean; Record the conversation of your call. The RecordingUrl will be sent to the StatusCallback URL if this is set to 'true' and the call conversation happens. Can be:

true - Call conversation will be recorded.
false (default) - Call conversation will not be recorded.
Note:- If this optional parameter is not passed then by default, calls will NOT be recorded. 

RecordingChannels Optional 
String; Number of audio channels to be present in the final recording. This parameter works if Record is set to 'true'. Can be:

single (default) - Record both legs of the call in a single channel of the recording file.
dual - Record the caller and the callee into separate channels of the recording file.
RecordingFormat Optional 
String; Quality of the audio recording. This parameter works if Record is set to 'true'. Can be:

mp3 (default) - Standard bitrate recording
mp3-hq - Higher bitrate (32 kbps/channel )recording.
Note:- mp3-hq option is an on-demand feature. Please reach out to hello@exotel.com or your account manager to get it enabled for your account before using this option.

StreamUrl Optional 
URL that supports WebSocket where audio will be streamed unidirectional

StreamBegin Optional 
String; Describes the beginning of audio streaming- from the point when first user connection is established or once both the users connections are established.

Can be: 

at Leg1Connect
at Leg2Connect
CustomField Optional 
Any application specific value like order id that will be passed back as a parameter in StatusCallback (only via 'terminal' StatusCallbackEvent)

StartPlaybackToNew Optional 
String; The party that should listen the playback at the start of the call. Audio to be listened by agent or both customer and agent just before the call gets connected. Can be:

Callee (default) - Playback audio will be played to callee only.
Both - Playback audio will be played to both caller and callee.
StartPlaybackValueNew Optional 
String; URL for the audio to be played just before the call gets connected.

Configuration for audio file supported in this playback are:
Sample Rate = 8 kHz
Bit depth = 16 bit
Bit rate = 128 kbps
Channel = mono
File Format = wav

StatusCallback Optional String; An HTTP POST request will be made to this URL depending on what events are subscribed using ‘StatusCallbackEvents’. Refer here for complete list of parameters which will be sent to your endpoint.
StatusCallbackEvents New Optional 
Array; Call events for which we will send details to the URL as set in ‘StatusCallback’ parameter. Can be:

terminal - This event will be triggered once the call is terminated (with or without being answered). 
answered - This event will be triggered when each leg of the call is answered. One for the caller and one for the callee.
If no event is specified, we will send the default parameters as specified here. Currently, only ‘terminal’ and ‘answered’ event is supported but more events could be added in future.

StatusCallbackContentType New Optional 
String; The HTTP header ‘Content-Type’ using which the StatusCallback webhook will be triggered to your URL. Can be:

multipart/form-data (default)
application/json
AnsweredBy Parameter (Beta)
We’ve introduced a new parameter called AnsweredBy in the StatusCallbackEvents to help identify whether a call was answered by a human or a voicemail system. This feature is currently in beta and supports the following possible values:

Human – The call was answered by a person.

Machine – The call was answered by a voicemail or automated system.

NotSure – The system couldn’t confidently determine who answered.

At present, AnsweredBy is available only for the second-leg AMD (Answering Machine Detection) in the Connect Two Numbers API.

If you would like to use streaming via this API, please contact hello@exotel.in

Time in format YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss; Date and time at which the user initiated the API

To

Your customer's phone number as set in the API request. This number will be connected after `From`.

From

The phone number that was attempted to be called first.

PhoneNumberSid

This is your ExoPhone's unique identifier.

StartTime

Time in format YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss; Date and time when the call request was initiated to the operator

EndTime

Time in format YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss; Date and time when the call was completed

ConversationDuration

The duration for the time `From` and `To` phone numbers were on call in seconds.

Direction

Can be:

inbound - Incoming call
outbound-dial - Outbound calls from Exotel dashboard
outbound-api - All other Outbound calls (API, campaign etc.)
CustomField

The value that was passed in the CustomField parameter of the API (if set during the request) will be populated here.

Legs

An array which will denote detailed information about each leg attempt involved in the call.

Legs[i]: `i` denotes the index of the number in order it is attempted. If there are multiple numbers attempted, array’s length will be equal to total attempts. In case of outgoing call connecting two numbers, `i` will be have possible values of 0 and 1. 0th index will represent 'From' leg and 1st index will be represent 'To' leg.
OnCallDuration: Indicates the duration that this leg was on a call. This value could be 0 if the call was not picked up by the respective leg.
RingingDuration: Indicates the duration of ringing time on each leg. This value could be 0 if it is a failed call.
Status: This denotes the terminal status of the particular leg of the call. Can be:
completed - The call was answered by the leg.
busy - A busy signal was returned by the leg.
failed - The call could not be completed as dialled, most likely because the phone number was non-existent.
no-answer - The call ended without being answered.
canceled - The call was canceled while queued or ringing.
null (empty) - The call to that leg was not even attempted.
For understanding more about leg-wise call status, refer here.

AnsweredBy: Indicates whether the call was answered by a Human, a Machine (e.g voicemail), or is Not Sure; this parameter is currently supported only for the second leg of the call when 'terminal' is subscribed to.
Sample:
Legs[0][OnCallDuration] = 45

Legs[0][RingingDuration] = 47

Legs[0][Status] = "completed"

Legs[0][AnsweredBy] = "NA"

Legs[1][OnCallDuration] = 16

Legs[1][RingingDuration] = 36

Legs[1][Status] = "completed"

Legs[1][AnsweredBy] = "HUMAN"

Additional StatusCallback fields are currently only supported if both ‘From’ and ‘To’ are set. StatusCallbackEvents parameter is not applicable for this case i.e. if ‘VoiceUrl’ is used. However, passthru applet can be utilised if ‘VoiceUrl’ is used.

-d "From=+91941374XXXX" \
-d "To=+91886799XXXX" \
-d "CallerId=0113083XXXX" \
-d "StatusCallback=http://your-application.com/exotel-callback" \
-d "StatusCallbackEvents[0]=terminal" \
-d "StatusCallbackContentType=application/json"

Outgoing call to connect number to a call flow
This API will first call the From number, and once they pick up the phone, it will connect them to a call flow (aka applet) that you have created in the system - like your landing app, or any other app that can play a greeting, have IVR, etc. For more details on setting up your flow, please refer Appplet documentation. An HTTP POST request is made to

POST
https://<your_api_key>:<your_api_token><subdomain>/v1/Accounts/<your_sid>/Calls/connectCopy
Try it
If you’d prefer response in JSON format, just append .json at the end of the HTTP POST request.

Replace <your_api_key> and <your_api_token> with the API key and token created by you.
Replace <your_sid> with your “Account sid”
Replace <subdomain> with the region of your account
<subdomain> of Singapore cluster is @api.exotel.com
<subdomain> of Mumbai cluster is @api.in.exotel.com
<your_api_key> , <your_api_token> and <your_sid> are available in the API settings page of your Exotel Dashboard

The following are the POST parameters:

Parameter Name

Mandatory/Optional

Value

From

Mandatory

The phone number that will be called first. Preferably in E.164 format. If not set, our system will try to match it with a country and make a call. If landline number, prefix it with STD code; Ex: 0XXXXXX2400

CallerId

Mandatory

This is your ExoPhone (pick one from here)

Url

Mandatory

http://my.exotel.com/{your_sid}/exoml/start_voice/{app_id} where app_id is the identiﬁer of the flow (or applet) that you want to connect to once the From number picks up the call. You can get the app_id from your Exotel Dashboard

CallType

Optional

trans - for Transactional Calls

TimeLimit

Optional

The time limit (in seconds) that you want this call to last. The call will be cut after this time (max. 14400 i.e. 4 hours)

TimeOut

Optional

The time (in seconds) to ring the called parties (both first and second call leg)

StatusCallback

Optional

When the call completes, an HTTP POST will be made to the provided URL with the following four parameters:

CallSid - an alpha-numeric unique identifier
Status - one of: completed, failed, busy, no-answer
RecordingUrl - link to the call recording (if it exists)
DateUpdated - time when the call state was updated last
CustomField

Optional

Any application specific value that will be passed back as a parameter while doing a GET request to the URL mentioned in your Passthru Applet or Greetings Applet.

Example Request
cURL
NodeJS
PHP
Python
Ruby
import requests

data = {
 'From': 'XXXXX30240',
 'CallerId': '0XXXXXX4890',
 'Url': 'http://my.exotel.com/Exotel/exoml/start_voice/926'
}

requests.post('https://<your_api_key>:<your_api_token><subdomain>/v1/Accounts/<your_sid>/Calls/connect', data=data)

The below query parameter in GET Call Details allows per-request control over the TTL (Time-To-Live) of the PreSignedRecordingUrl. It accepts values between 5 to 60 minutes, overriding the account-level setting for more granular access control.

Parameter Name Mandatory / Optional Value

Please make sure to URL encode query parameters in the HTTP GET request.

If you would like to use the pre-signed URL via this API, please contact hello@exotel.in

Description of request query parameters (filters):

Parameter Name Description
Sid 
string; an alpha-numeric unique identifier of the call

One or multiple Call SIDs which are comma separated. Recommended limit of SIDs which should be passed together is 20 and maximum allowed limit is 100. If DateCreated is not set, it will only check for last 31 days by default. While querying Sid(s) older than 31 days, DateCreated filter needs to be provided.

 

Example:
/Calls?Sid=48d690c837bb0c755a1228dcb6911416,d7d9cefd9773dd746d8f1e029cdb1417
/Calls?Sid=48d690c837bb0c755a1228dcb6911416&DateCreated=gte:2019-01-01 00:00:00;lte:2019-01-31 23:59:59

DateCreated Date and time at which the Call resource was created in the Exotel system. Supported operators (gte and lte), for more info refer to filter operators section below. You can query call records only up to 6 months old and provide maximum date range of 1 month.

Default if not set: Last 31 days

Example:
/Calls?DateCreated=gte:2019-01-01 00:00:00;lte:2019-01-31 23:59:59
To Your customer's phone number. One or multiple To numbers can be provided (in E.164 format) which are comma separated. (max limit: 5)

Example:
/Calls?To=<number-1>
/Calls?To=<number-1>,<number-2>"
From The phone number that will be called first. One or multiple From numbers can be provided (in E.164 format) which are comma separated. (max limit: 5)

Example:
/Calls?From=<number-1>
/Calls?From=<number-1>,<number-2>,...
Status 
Overall call status, which could be one of:

completed - The call was answered and has ended normally
failed - The call could not be completed as dialled, most likely because the phone number was non-existent
busy - The caller received a busy signal
no-answer - The call ended without being answered
Example:
/Calls?Status=completed
/Calls?Status=failed,no-answer,busy,canceled

Duration Call duration in seconds. Supported operators (gte, eq and lte), for more info refer to filter operators section below.

Example:
/Calls?Duration=gte:10s;lte:45s
/Calls?Duration=eq:30s
Price If present, this will be the amount (as per your billing currency) you have been charged for the call. Supported operators (gte, eq and lte), for more info refer to filter operators section below.

Example:
/Calls?Price=gte:0.10;lte:1.0
/Calls?Price=eq:0.300030
Direction 
inbound
outbound-dial - Outbound calls from Exotel dashboard
outbound-api - All other Outbound calls (API, campaign etc.)
Example:
/Calls?Direction=inbound
/Calls?Direction=outbound-dial,inbound

PhoneNumber This represents the Virtual Number (ExoPhone) used for the call. One or multiple PhoneNumber(s) can be provided (in E.164 format) which are comma separated. (max limit: 5)

Example:
/Calls?PhoneNumber=<vn-1>
/Calls?PhoneNumber=<vn-1>,<vn-2>,...
PageSize This represents number of records visible in one page of the API response. Default: 50, Max: 100
SortBy This indicates in what order the Call records are sorted in the API response. By default records are sorted by DateCreated in descending order. However, you can override the same in following way for ascending order:

Example:
/Calls?SortBy=DateCreated:asc
Before Auto generated unique string returned in the PrevPageUri (under Metadata) to be used as query param when at least one record is returned in that page. The value of this field is a cursor which identifies a call record uniquely.
After Auto generated unique string returned in the NextPageUri (under Metadata) to be used as query param when at least one record is present in that page. The value of this field is a cursor which identifies a call record uniquely.
Filter Operators (Please note these operators are only applicable to certain query parameters as mentioned above)

Operator

Description

Examples

eq:

Equals

Return results where duration is exactly ten seconds:

Duration=eq:10s

Same can also be written as Duration=10s

gte:

Greater than or equal to

Return results where Duration is ten seconds or more:

Duration=gte:10s

lte:

Less than or equal to

Return results where Duration is ten seconds or less:

Duration=lte:10s

,

OR operator

OR operator (,) is used to select multiple values if any one of them matches

;

AND operator

AND operator (;) is used to select multiple values if all of them matches. Url encode ; to %3B while making the API request.

StatusCallBack delivery may be delayed or have failures due to multiple reasons like – network connectivity, customer web hook uptime, server failures, etc. Customers are advised to implement fallback to call details API for fetching the call status. 

Exotel will perform an asynchronous HTTP request to the StatusCallback URL you have specified in your request (if any) once the call completes. List of parameters which will be sent as part of StatusCallback:

An array which will denote detailed information about each leg attempt involved in the call.

Legs[i]: `i` denotes the index of the number in order it is attempted. If there are multiple numbers attempted, array’s length will be equal to total attempts. In case of outgoing call connecting two numbers, `i` will be have possible values of 0 and 1. 0th index will represent 'From' leg and 1st index will be represent 'To' leg.

To build a robust integration for your new feature, we will name this microservice: PSTN-Stream-Relay-Service . 

 This service handles three things: 

 Call Initiation: Triggering the connection between numbers. 

 Real-time Streaming: A WebSocket server to receive live audio packets. 

 Post-Call Processing: A webhook to receive and store the final recording URL. 

 1. Requirements 

 You will need to install these libraries: 

 pip install fastapi uvicorn requests python-multipart

 2. Implementation Scripts 

 File: config.py 

 API_KEY = "your_api_key"
API_TOKEN = "your_api_token"
ACCOUNT_SID = "your_sid"
SUBDOMAIN = "api.in.exotel.com"
BASE_URL = f"https://{API_KEY}:{API_TOKEN}@{SUBDOMAIN}/v1/Accounts/{ACCOUNT_SID}/Calls/connect.json"

SERVER_URL = "https://your-public-domain.com"
STREAM_URL = "wss://your-public-domain.com/audio-stream"

 File: exotel_logic.py 

 import requests
import config

def trigger_connect_call(agent_num, customer_num, virtual_num):
 payload = {
 "From": agent_num,
 "To": customer_num,
 "CallerId": virtual_num,
 "Record": "true",
 "StreamUrl": config.STREAM_URL,
 "StreamBegin": "atLeg2Connect",
 "StatusCallback": f"{config.SERVER_URL}/callback",
 "StatusCallbackEvents[0]": "terminal",
 "StatusCallbackContentType": "application/json"
 }

 response = requests.post(config.BASE_URL, data=payload)
 return response.json()

 File: main.py 

 from fastapi import FastAPI, WebSocket, Request
import exotel_logic

app = FastAPI()

@app.post("/start-call")
async def start_call(agent: str, customer: str, vn: str):
 result = exotel_logic.trigger_connect_call(agent, customer, vn)
 return result

@app.websocket("/audio-stream")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket):
 await websocket.accept()
 while True:
 data = await websocket.receive_bytes()
 print(f"Received audio packet: {len(data)} bytes")

@app.post("/callback")
async def call_callback(request: Request):
 data = await request.json()
 recording_url = data.get("RecordingUrl")
 call_sid = data.get("CallSid")

 if recording_url:
 print(f"Final recording for {call_sid}: {recording_url}")

Outgoing call to connect two numbers
Voice v1 APIs work without any user (call centre agent) context, i.e. they don’t need a user to be added to the Exotel dashboard and therefore don’t check a user number for busy status before calling that number.

This API will connect two numbers. It connects From Number first. Once the person at the From end picks up the phone, it will connect to the number provided as To. You can choose which number should be connected first by adding that number in the From field. An HTTP POST request is made to

POST
https://<your_api_key>:<your_api_token><subdomain>/v1/Accounts/<your_sid>/Calls/connectCopy
Try it
If you’d prefer response in JSON format, just append .json at the end of the HTTP POST request.

Replace <your_api_key> and <your_api_token> with the API key and token created by you.

Replace <your_sid> with your “Account sid”
Replace <subdomain> with the region of your account
<subdomain> of Singapore cluster is @api.exotel.com
<subdomain> of Mumbai cluster is @api.in.exotel.com
<your_api_key> , <your_api_token> and <your_sid> are available in the API settings page of your Exotel Dashboard

The following are the POST parameters sent as form-data in the Body of the Request:

Parameter Name Mandatory / Optional Value
From Mandatory String; The phone number that will be called first. Preferably in E.164 format. If not set, our system will try to match it with a country and make a call. If landline number, prefix it with STD code; Ex: 080XXXX2400
To Mandatory String; Your customer's phone number. If landline number, prefix it with STD code; Ex: 080XXXX2400
CallerId Mandatory String; This is your ExoPhone/Exotel Virtual Number (pick one from here)
CallType Optional String; trans - for Transactional Calls
TimeLimit Optional Integer; The time limit (in seconds) that you want this call to last. The call will be cut after this time (max. 14400 i.e. 4 hours)
TimeOut Optional Integer; The time (in seconds) to ring the called parties (both first and second call leg)
WaitUrl Optional 
String; Play this audio to the caller. When the first leg (From) has to wait for the other leg (To) to pick up the call, the audio file specified in this parameter will be played.

Please refer this article to understand the format specifications of the audio file to be played (wav is only supported).

Guidelines on usage:

The audio file size is recommended to be less than 2MB. Please note, Exotel will cache the wav file. During the first few call attempts of setting this parameter, user might hear normal ringing tone for first 5 seconds (for a ~2MB file). This is only temporary for initial few calls and once the audio file is cached, audio will be played out smoothly.
In case you decide to change the audio file later, the WaitUrl should be different (as Exotel will cache audio file based on URL). You can do so by hosting the audio file with a different name.
When using this parameter, it is recommended to set the TimeOut parameter as well.
Example: "http://{your_hosted_endpoint}/{audio file name}.wav"

Record Optional 
Boolean; Record the conversation of your call. The RecordingUrl will be sent to the StatusCallback URL if this is set to 'true' and the call conversation happens. Can be:

true - Call conversation will be recorded.
false (default) - Call conversation will not be recorded.
Note:- If this optional parameter is not passed then by default, calls will NOT be recorded. 

RecordingChannels Optional 
String; Number of audio channels to be present in the final recording. This parameter works if Record is set to 'true'. Can be:

single (default) - Record both legs of the call in a single channel of the recording file.
dual - Record the caller and the callee into separate channels of the recording file.
RecordingFormat Optional 
String; Quality of the audio recording. This parameter works if Record is set to 'true'. Can be:

mp3 (default) - Standard bitrate recording
mp3-hq - Higher bitrate (32 kbps/channel )recording.
Note:- mp3-hq option is an on-demand feature. Please reach out to hello@exotel.com or your account manager to get it enabled for your account before using this option.

StreamUrl Optional 
URL that supports WebSocket where audio will be streamed unidirectional

StreamBegin Optional 
String; Describes the beginning of audio streaming- from the point when first user connection is established or once both the users connections are established.

Can be: 

at Leg1Connect
at Leg2Connect
CustomField Optional 
Any application specific value like order id that will be passed back as a parameter in StatusCallback (only via 'terminal' StatusCallbackEvent)

StartPlaybackToNew Optional 
String; The party that should listen the playback at the start of the call. Audio to be listened by agent or both customer and agent just before the call gets connected. Can be:

Callee (default) - Playback audio will be played to callee only.
Both - Playback audio will be played to both caller and callee.
StartPlaybackValueNew Optional 
String; URL for the audio to be played just before the call gets connected.

Configuration for audio file supported in this playback are:
Sample Rate = 8 kHz
Bit depth = 16 bit
Bit rate = 128 kbps
Channel = mono
File Format = wav

StatusCallback Optional String; An HTTP POST request will be made to this URL depending on what events are subscribed using ‘StatusCallbackEvents’. Refer here for complete list of parameters which will be sent to your endpoint.
StatusCallbackEvents New Optional 
Array; Call events for which we will send details to the URL as set in ‘StatusCallback’ parameter. Can be:

terminal - This event will be triggered once the call is terminated (with or without being answered). 
answered - This event will be triggered when each leg of the call is answered. One for the caller and one for the callee.
If no event is specified, we will send the default parameters as specified here. Currently, only ‘terminal’ and ‘answered’ event is supported but more events could be added in future.

StatusCallbackContentType New Optional 
String; The HTTP header ‘Content-Type’ using which the StatusCallback webhook will be triggered to your URL. Can be:

multipart/form-data (default)
application/json
AnsweredBy Parameter (Beta)
We’ve introduced a new parameter called AnsweredBy in the StatusCallbackEvents to help identify whether a call was answered by a human or a voicemail system. This feature is currently in beta and supports the following possible values:

Human – The call was answered by a person.

Machine – The call was answered by a voicemail or automated system.

NotSure – The system couldn’t confidently determine who answered.

At present, AnsweredBy is available only for the second-leg AMD (Answering Machine Detection) in the Connect Two Numbers API.

If you would like to use streaming via this API, please contact hello@exotel.in

Exotel will perform an asynchronous HTTP request to the StatusCallback URL you have specified in your request (if any) once the call completes. List of parameters which will be sent as part of StatusCallback:

 

Parameter Name Type & Value
CallSid string; an alpha-numeric unique identifier of the call
DateUpdated Time in format YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss; Date and time at which the status of the call was last updated in our system

List of additional fields which will be sent if 'terminal' and/or ‘answered’ event is subscribed using 'StatusCallbackEvents' in the request:

Parameter Name

Type & Value

EventType

String; This will be the type of event for which 'StatusCallback' is triggered for and subscribed using 'StatusCallbackEvents'.

Currently, only ‘terminal’ and ‘answered’ as an event are supported. However, more events can be added in the future.

DateCreated

Time in format YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss; Date and time at which the user initiated the API

To

Your customer's phone number as set in the API request. This number will be connected after `From`.

From

The phone number that was attempted to be called first.

PhoneNumberSid

This is your ExoPhone's unique identifier.

StartTime

Time in format YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss; Date and time when the call request was initiated to the operator

EndTime

Time in format YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss; Date and time when the call was completed

ConversationDuration

The duration for the time `From` and `To` phone numbers were on call in seconds.

Direction

Can be:

inbound - Incoming call
outbound-dial - Outbound calls from Exotel dashboard
outbound-api - All other Outbound calls (API, campaign etc.)
CustomField

The value that was passed in the CustomField parameter of the API (if set during the request) will be populated here.

Legs

An array which will denote detailed information about each leg attempt involved in the call.

Legs[i]: `i` denotes the index of the number in order it is attempted. If there are multiple numbers attempted, array’s length will be equal to total attempts. In case of outgoing call connecting two numbers, `i` will be have possible values of 0 and 1. 0th index will represent 'From' leg and 1st index will be represent 'To' leg.
OnCallDuration: Indicates the duration that this leg was on a call. This value could be 0 if the call was not picked up by the respective leg.
RingingDuration: Indicates the duration of ringing time on each leg. This value could be 0 if it is a failed call.
Status: This denotes the terminal status of the particular leg of the call. Can be:
completed - The call was answered by the leg.
busy - A busy signal was returned by the leg.
failed - The call could not be completed as dialled, most likely because the phone number was non-existent.
no-answer - The call ended without being answered.
canceled - The call was canceled while queued or ringing.
null (empty) - The call to that leg was not even attempted.
For understanding more about leg-wise call status, refer here.

AnsweredBy: Indicates whether the call was answered by a Human, a Machine (e.g voicemail), or is Not Sure; this parameter is currently supported only for the second leg of the call when 'terminal' is subscribed to.

Legs[0][OnCallDuration] = 45

Legs[0][RingingDuration] = 47

Legs[0][Status] = "completed"

Legs[0][AnsweredBy] = "NA"

Legs[1][OnCallDuration] = 16

Legs[1][RingingDuration] = 36

Legs[1][Status] = "completed"

Legs[1][AnsweredBy] = "HUMAN"

Additional StatusCallback fields are currently only supported if both ‘From’ and ‘To’ are set. StatusCallbackEvents parameter is not applicable for this case i.e. if ‘VoiceUrl’ is used. However, passthru applet can be utilised if ‘VoiceUrl’ is used.

Call Details
To get details of a call (including Status, Price, etc.), you will need to make a HTTP GET request to

GET
https://<your_api_key>:<your_api_token><subdomain>/v1/Accounts/<your_sid>/Calls/<CallSid>Copy
Try it
Where <CallSid> is an alpha-numeric unique identifier generated for all the calls made via Exotel.

If you’d prefer response in JSON format, just append .json at the end of the HTTP GET request.

Replace <your_api_key> and <your_api_token> with the API key and token created by you.
Replace <your_sid> with your “Account sid”
Replace <subdomain> with the region of your account
<subdomain> of Singapore cluster is @api.exotel.com
<subdomain> of Mumbai cluster is @api.in.exotel.com
<your_api_key> , <your_api_token> and <your_sid> are available in the API settings page of your Exotel Dashboard

In the case of an outbound call originated via the API, the Sid parameter is as returned in the XML/JSON response to your request. In the case of inbound calls, you can get the Sid by using the Passthru applet.

The below query parameter in GET Call Details allows per-request control over the TTL (Time-To-Live) of the PreSignedRecordingUrl. It accepts values between 5 to 60 minutes, overriding the account-level setting for more granular access control.

Parameter Name Mandatory / Optional Value
RecordingUrlValidity Optional An Integer equal to or between 5 and 60.
Note- If the value is greater than 60 or less than 5 then it will return a 4XX Error.
If you would like to use the pre-signed URL via this API, please contact hello@exotel.in

 from fastapi import FastAPI, Form, WebSocket, WebSocketDisconnect
import requests

app = FastAPI()

# --- CONFIGURATION ---
API_KEY = "your_api_key"
API_TOKEN = "your_api_token"
ACCOUNT_SID = "your_sid"
SUBDOMAIN = "api.in.exotel.com" # Mumbai Cluster for India Compliance
BASE_URL = "https://your-public-domain.com" # Replace with your ngrok/server URL

# --- 1. TRIGGER CALL ---
@app.post("/make-call")
def trigger_exotel_call(agent_phone: str, customer_phone: str, virtual_number: str):
 url = f"https://{API_KEY}:{API_TOKEN}@{SUBDOMAIN}/v1/Accounts/{ACCOUNT_SID}/Calls/connect.json"

 payload = {
 "From": agent_phone,
 "To": customer_phone,
 "CallerId": virtual_number,
 "Record": "true", # Ensures we get the final recording
 "StreamUrl": f"{BASE_URL.replace('https', 'wss')}/ws/audio", # Real-time stream
 "StreamBegin": "atLeg2Connect", # Starts streaming when customer picks up
 "StatusCallback": f"{BASE_URL}/callback", # Where final recording URL is sent
 "StatusCallbackEvents[0]": "terminal"
 }

 response = requests.post(url, data=payload)
 return response.json()

# --- 2. REAL-TIME PACKET RECEIVER (WebSocket) ---
@app.websocket("/ws/audio")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket):
 await websocket.accept()
 try:
 while True:
 # Exotel sends audio packets as binary/json through this connection
 data = await websocket.receive_bytes()
 # Process your real-time packets here (e.g., AI Transcriptions)
 print(f"Received audio packet: {len(data)} bytes")
 except WebSocketDisconnect:
 print("Real-time stream disconnected")

# --- 3. FINAL RECORDING CALLBACK ---
@app.post("/callback")
async def exotel_callback(
 CallSid: str = Form(...), 
 Status: str = Form(...), 
 RecordingUrl: str = Form(None)
):
 if RecordingUrl:
 print(f"Call {CallSid} ended. Final recording: {RecordingUrl}")
 # Save RecordingUrl to your database here
 return {"status": "ok"}

if __name__ == "__main__":
 import uvicorn

Outgoing call to connect two numbers
Voice v1 APIs work without any user (call centre agent) context, i.e. they don’t need a user to be added to the Exotel dashboard and therefore don’t check a user number for busy status before calling that number.

This API will connect two numbers. It connects From Number first. Once the person at the From end picks up the phone, it will connect to the number provided as To. You can choose which number should be connected first by adding that number in the From field. An HTTP POST request is made to

POST
https://<your_api_key>:<your_api_token><subdomain>/v1/Accounts/<your_sid>/Calls/connectCopy
Try it
If you’d prefer response in JSON format, just append .json at the end of the HTTP POST request.

Replace <your_api_key> and <your_api_token> with the API key and token created by you.

Replace <your_sid> with your “Account sid”
Replace <subdomain> with the region of your account
<subdomain> of Singapore cluster is @api.exotel.com
<subdomain> of Mumbai cluster is @api.in.exotel.com
<your_api_key> , <your_api_token> and <your_sid> are available in the API settings page of your Exotel Dashboard

The following are the POST parameters sent as form-data in the Body of the Request:

Parameter Name Mandatory / Optional Value
From Mandatory String; The phone number that will be called first. Preferably in E.164 format. If not set, our system will try to match it with a country and make a call. If landline number, prefix it with STD code; Ex: 080XXXX2400
To Mandatory String; Your customer's phone number. If landline number, prefix it with STD code; Ex: 080XXXX2400
CallerId Mandatory String; This is your ExoPhone/Exotel Virtual Number (pick one from here)
CallType Optional String; trans - for Transactional Calls
TimeLimit Optional Integer; The time limit (in seconds) that you want this call to last. The call will be cut after this time (max. 14400 i.e. 4 hours)
TimeOut Optional Integer; The time (in seconds) to ring the called parties (both first and second call leg)
WaitUrl Optional 
String; Play this audio to the caller. When the first leg (From) has to wait for the other leg (To) to pick up the call, the audio file specified in this parameter will be played.

Please refer this article to understand the format specifications of the audio file to be played (wav is only supported).

Guidelines on usage:

The audio file size is recommended to be less than 2MB. Please note, Exotel will cache the wav file. During the first few call attempts of setting this parameter, user might hear normal ringing tone for first 5 seconds (for a ~2MB file). This is only temporary for initial few calls and once the audio file is cached, audio will be played out smoothly.
In case you decide to change the audio file later, the WaitUrl should be different (as Exotel will cache audio file based on URL). You can do so by hosting the audio file with a different name.
When using this parameter, it is recommended to set the TimeOut parameter as well.
Example: "http://{your_hosted_endpoint}/{audio file name}.wav"

Record Optional 
Boolean; Record the conversation of your call. The RecordingUrl will be sent to the StatusCallback URL if this is set to 'true' and the call conversation happens. Can be:

true - Call conversation will be recorded.
false (default) - Call conversation will not be recorded.
Note:- If this optional parameter is not passed then by default, calls will NOT be recorded. 

RecordingChannels Optional 
String; Number of audio channels to be present in the final recording. This parameter works if Record is set to 'true'. Can be:

single (default) - Record both legs of the call in a single channel of the recording file.
dual - Record the caller and the callee into separate channels of the recording file.
RecordingFormat Optional 
String; Quality of the audio recording. This parameter works if Record is set to 'true'. Can be:

mp3 (default) - Standard bitrate recording
mp3-hq - Higher bitrate (32 kbps/channel )recording.
Note:- mp3-hq option is an on-demand feature. Please reach out to hello@exotel.com or your account manager to get it enabled for your account before using this option.

StreamUrl Optional 
URL that supports WebSocket where audio will be streamed unidirectional

StreamBegin Optional 
String; Describes the beginning of audio streaming- from the point when first user connection is established or once both the users connections are established.

Can be: 

at Leg1Connect
at Leg2Connect
CustomField Optional 
Any application specific value like order id that will be passed back as a parameter in StatusCallback (only via 'terminal' StatusCallbackEvent)

StartPlaybackToNew Optional 
String; The party that should listen the playback at the start of the call. Audio to be listened by agent or both customer and agent just before the call gets connected. Can be:

Callee (default) - Playback audio will be played to callee only.
Both - Playback audio will be played to both caller and callee.
StartPlaybackValueNew Optional 
String; URL for the audio to be played just before the call gets connected.

Configuration for audio file supported in this playback are:
Sample Rate = 8 kHz
Bit depth = 16 bit
Bit rate = 128 kbps
Channel = mono
File Format = wav

StatusCallback Optional String; An HTTP POST request will be made to this URL depending on what events are subscribed using ‘StatusCallbackEvents’. Refer here for complete list of parameters which will be sent to your endpoint.
StatusCallbackEvents New Optional 
Array; Call events for which we will send details to the URL as set in ‘StatusCallback’ parameter. Can be:

terminal - This event will be triggered once the call is terminated (with or without being answered). 
answered - This event will be triggered when each leg of the call is answered. One for the caller and one for the callee.
If no event is specified, we will send the default parameters as specified here. Currently, only ‘terminal’ and ‘answered’ event is supported but more events could be added in future.

StatusCallbackContentType New Optional 
String; The HTTP header ‘Content-Type’ using which the StatusCallback webhook will be triggered to your URL. Can be:

multipart/form-data (default)
application/json
AnsweredBy Parameter (Beta)
We’ve introduced a new parameter called AnsweredBy in the StatusCallbackEvents to help identify whether a call was answered by a human or a voicemail system. This feature is currently in beta and supports the following possible values:

Human – The call was answered by a person.

Machine – The call was answered by a voicemail or automated system.

NotSure – The system couldn’t confidently determine who answered.

At present, AnsweredBy is available only for the second-leg AMD (Answering Machine Detection) in the Connect Two Numbers API.

If you would like to use streaming via this API, please contact hello@exotel.in

Outgoing call to connect number to a call flow
This API will first call the From number, and once they pick up the phone, it will connect them to a call flow (aka applet) that you have created in the system - like your landing app, or any other app that can play a greeting, have IVR, etc. For more details on setting up your flow, please refer Appplet documentation. An HTTP POST request is made to

POST
https://<your_api_key>:<your_api_token><subdomain>/v1/Accounts/<your_sid>/Calls/connectCopy
Try it
If you’d prefer response in JSON format, just append .json at the end of the HTTP POST request.

Replace <your_api_key> and <your_api_token> with the API key and token created by you.
Replace <your_sid> with your “Account sid”
Replace <subdomain> with the region of your account
<subdomain> of Singapore cluster is @api.exotel.com
<subdomain> of Mumbai cluster is @api.in.exotel.com
<your_api_key> , <your_api_token> and <your_sid> are available in the API settings page of your Exotel Dashboard

The following are the POST parameters:

Parameter Name

Mandatory/Optional

Value

From

Mandatory

The phone number that will be called first. Preferably in E.164 format. If not set, our system will try to match it with a country and make a call. If landline number, prefix it with STD code; Ex: 0XXXXXX2400

CallerId

Mandatory

This is your ExoPhone (pick one from here)

Url

Mandatory

http://my.exotel.com/{your_sid}/exoml/start_voice/{app_id} where app_id is the identiﬁer of the flow (or applet) that you want to connect to once the From number picks up the call. You can get the app_id from your Exotel Dashboard

CallType

Optional

trans - for Transactional Calls

TimeLimit

Optional

The time limit (in seconds) that you want this call to last. The call will be cut after this time (max. 14400 i.e. 4 hours)

TimeOut

Optional

The time (in seconds) to ring the called parties (both first and second call leg)

StatusCallback

Optional

When the call completes, an HTTP POST will be made to the provided URL with the following four parameters:

CallSid - an alpha-numeric unique identifier
Status - one of: completed, failed, busy, no-answer
RecordingUrl - link to the call recording (if it exists)
DateUpdated - time when the call state was updated last
CustomField

Optional

Any application specific value that will be passed back as a parameter while doing a GET request to the URL mentioned in your Passthru Applet or Greetings Applet.

Example Request
cURL
NodeJS
PHP
Python
Ruby
import requests

data = {
 'From': 'XXXXX30240',
 'CallerId': '0XXXXXX4890',
 'Url': 'http://my.exotel.com/Exotel/exoml/start_voice/926'
}

requests.post('https://<your_api_key>:<your_api_token><subdomain>/v1/Accounts/<your_sid>/Calls/connect', data=data)

Description of request query parameters (filters):

Parameter Name Description
Sid 
string; an alpha-numeric unique identifier of the call

One or multiple Call SIDs which are comma separated. Recommended limit of SIDs which should be passed together is 20 and maximum allowed limit is 100. If DateCreated is not set, it will only check for last 31 days by default. While querying Sid(s) older than 31 days, DateCreated filter needs to be provided.

 

Example:
/Calls?Sid=48d690c837bb0c755a1228dcb6911416,d7d9cefd9773dd746d8f1e029cdb1417

DateCreated Date and time at which the Call resource was created in the Exotel system. Supported operators (gte and lte), for more info refer to filter operators section below. You can query call records only up to 6 months old and provide maximum date range of 1 month.

Default if not set: Last 31 days

Example:
/Calls?DateCreated=gte:2019-01-01 00:00:00;lte:2019-01-31 23:59:59
To Your customer's phone number. One or multiple To numbers can be provided (in E.164 format) which are comma separated. (max limit: 5)

Example:
/Calls?To=<number-1>
/Calls?To=<number-1>,<number-2>"
From The phone number that will be called first. One or multiple From numbers can be provided (in E.164 format) which are comma separated. (max limit: 5)

Example:
/Calls?From=<number-1>
/Calls?From=<number-1>,<number-2>,...
Status 
Overall call status, which could be one of:

completed - The call was answered and has ended normally
failed - The call could not be completed as dialled, most likely because the phone number was non-existent
busy - The caller received a busy signal
no-answer - The call ended without being answered
Example:
/Calls?Status=completed
/Calls?Status=failed,no-answer,busy,canceled

Duration Call duration in seconds. Supported operators (gte, eq and lte), for more info refer to filter operators section below.

Example:
/Calls?Duration=gte:10s;lte:45s
/Calls?Duration=eq:30s
Price If present, this will be the amount (as per your billing currency) you have been charged for the call. Supported operators (gte, eq and lte), for more info refer to filter operators section below.

Example:
/Calls?Price=gte:0.10;lte:1.0
/Calls?Price=eq:0.300030
Direction 
inbound
outbound-dial - Outbound calls from Exotel dashboard
outbound-api - All other Outbound calls (API, campaign etc.)
Example:
/Calls?Direction=inbound
/Calls?Direction=outbound-dial,inbound

PhoneNumber This represents the Virtual Number (ExoPhone) used for the call. One or multiple PhoneNumber(s) can be provided (in E.164 format) which are comma separated. (max limit: 5)

Example:
/Calls?PhoneNumber=<vn-1>
/Calls?PhoneNumber=<vn-1>,<vn-2>,...
PageSize This represents number of records visible in one page of the API response. Default: 50, Max: 100
SortBy This indicates in what order the Call records are sorted in the API response. By default records are sorted by DateCreated in descending order. However, you can override the same in following way for ascending order:

Example:
/Calls?SortBy=DateCreated:asc
Before Auto generated unique string returned in the PrevPageUri (under Metadata) to be used as query param when at least one record is returned in that page. The value of this field is a cursor which identifies a call record uniquely.
After Auto generated unique string returned in the NextPageUri (under Metadata) to be used as query param when at least one record is present in that page. The value of this field is a cursor which identifies a call record uniquely.
Filter Operators (Please note these operators are only applicable to certain query parameters as mentioned above)

Operator

Description

Examples

eq:

Equals

Return results where duration is exactly ten seconds:

Duration=eq:10s

Same can also be written as Duration=10s

gte:

Greater than or equal to

Return results where Duration is ten seconds or more:

Duration=gte:10s

lte:

Less than or equal to

Return results where Duration is ten seconds or less:

Duration=lte:10s

,

OR operator

OR operator (,) is used to select multiple values if any one of them matches

;

AND operator

AND operator (;) is used to select multiple values if all of them matches. Url encode ; to %3B while making the API request.

 FastAPI Service Implementation

 from fastapi import FastAPI, Form
import requests

app = FastAPI()

API_KEY = "your_api_key"
API_TOKEN = "your_api_token"
SUBDOMAIN = "api.in.exotel.com"
ACCOUNT_SID = "your_sid"

@app.post("/initiate-call")
def make_call(customer_number: str, agent_number: str, virtual_number: str):
 url = f"https://{API_KEY}:{API_TOKEN}@{SUBDOMAIN}/v1/Accounts/{ACCOUNT_SID}/Calls/connect.json"

 payload = {
 "From": agent_number,
 "To": customer_number,
 "CallerId": virtual_number,
 "StreamUrl": "wss://your-websocket-server.com/audio",
 "StreamBegin": "atLeg2Connect",
 "Record": "true"
 }

 response = requests.post(url, data=payload)
 return response.json()

@app.post("/exotel-callback")
def handle_callback(CallSid: str = Form(...), Status: str = Form(...)):
 return {"status": "received", "call_id": CallSid, "state": Status}

 Feature Implementation Detail 
 Data Residency Use api.in.exotel.com to ensure data remains in the Mumbai region. 
 Real-time Audio Use the StreamUrl parameter with a WebSocket (WSS) endpoint. 
 PSTN Connection Exotel connects the From number first, then the To number over standard telecom lines. 
 Security Authentication is handled via Basic Auth in the URL string using your Key and Token. 

 How the process works: 

 Trigger: Your Python service calls the /initiate-call endpoint. 

 First Leg: Exotel dials the From number (your agent or system). 

 Second Leg: Once the first person answers, Exotel dials the To number (the customer). 

 Streaming: As soon as the customer ( Leg2 ) connects, Exotel starts pushing unidirectional audio packets to your StreamUrl . 

 Compliance: By using the Mumbai subdomain, your call logs and metadata are processed through Indian data centers.

 except Exception as e:
 return {"error": str(e)}

 def list_schema_tool(self):
 """

 """

 table_name, 
 column_name, 
 data_type 
 FROM 
 information_schema.columns 
 WHERE 
 table_schema = 'public'
 ORDER BY 
 table_name, 
 ordinal_position;
 """

 formatted_schema = "\n".join(
 [f"Table '{table}': {', '.join(cols)}" for table, cols in schema.items()]
 )
 return f"Database Schema:\n{formatted_schema}"

 def execute_query_tool(self, sql_query: str):
 """
 A tool to execute a given SQL query on the database.

 result = self._execute_query(sql_query)

 return f"Error executing query: {result['error']}"

 return f"Query Result:\nColumns: {result['columns']}\nData: {result['data']}"

 idea.md 

 The core idea for this problem, "Chroma's Journey," originated from a desire to create a shortest path problem with a twist that elevates it beyond a standard Dijkstra or Floyd-Warshall application. Standard shortest path algorithms operate on the principle that the cost to reach a vertex `v` is independent of the path taken, as long as the total path weight is minimized. I wanted to challenge this assumption.

**Initial Concept**

My first thought was to make edge weights dynamic. For instance, traversing an edge could permanently change its weight or the weights of adjacent edges. However, this often leads to very complex state spaces or problems that are too difficult for a typical competitive programming contest (e.g., potentially NP-hard).

**Refinement: Path-Dependent Costs**

I simplified the concept to "path-dependent costs." Instead of the edge weights themselves changing, the cost of traversing an edge would depend on the **immediately preceding** edge. This preserves a more structured state that can still be explored with graph algorithms.

**Introducing Colors**

To formalize this dependency, I introduced the concept of colored edges. This provides a clean, discrete way to categorize edges and define the dependencies. The cost of traversing an edge `(u, v)` of color `c_2` after arriving at `u` via an edge of color `c_1` could then be defined by a lookup in a transition cost matrix, `T[c_1][c_2]`.

**Final Formulation**

The problem was then formulated as finding the minimum cost path in a graph with these transition costs. The total cost of an edge traversal now has two components: its intrinsic weight and the transition cost. This leads to the key insight: a state in our search algorithm cannot just be the current vertex `v`. It must also include information about the edge used to arrive at `v`. The most concise way to represent this is the pair `(vertex, previous_edge_color)`. This transforms the problem into a shortest path problem on a larger, implicit "state graph," which is a classic technique for solving variations of shortest path problems. This felt like the right level of difficulty—it requires a non-trivial insight but relies on a standard algorithm (Dijkstra's) for the solution, making it suitable for a Div1/Div2 contest.

 problem.md 

 ## C. Chroma's Journey

Chroma is an artist who lives in a world of colored paths. Their city can be represented as a directed graph where each path (edge) has a specific color and an associated travel time (weight).

Chroma enjoys journeys that are aesthetically pleasing. The harmony of transitioning from one color to another affects the total "effort" of the trip. For any two colors, there's a specific "transition cost" associated with moving from a path of the first color to a path of the second color.

Your task is to help Chroma find the minimum total cost to travel from a starting point (vertex $S$) to a destination (vertex $T$). The total cost of a path is the sum of the travel times of all edges in the path, plus the sum of all transition costs incurred at each vertex along the path.

Note that the journey begins at vertex $S$, so the first edge taken has no preceding edge. Therefore, the transition cost for the first edge of the path is 0.

### Input

The first line contains five integers: $N$, $M$, $C$, $S$, and $T$.
* $N$: the number of vertices in the city ($2 \le N \le 10^5$)
* $M$: the number of directed edges (paths) in the city ($1 \le M \le 2 \cdot 10^5$)
* $C$: the number of colors ($1 \le C \le 50$)
* $S$: the starting vertex ($1 \le S \le N$)
* $T$: the destination vertex ($1 \le T \le N, S \ne T$)

The next $M$ lines describe the edges. Each line contains four integers: $u$, $v$, $c$, $w$.
* $u$, $v$: the start and end vertices of a directed edge ($1 \le u, v \le N$)
* $c$: the color of the edge ($1 \le c \le C$)
* $w$: the travel time (weight) of the edge ($1 \le w \le 1000$)

The next $C$ lines describe the transition costs. The $i$-th line contains $C$ integers. The $j$-th integer in the $i$-th line, $cost_{i,j}$, is the transition cost of moving from an edge of color $i$ to an edge of color $j$ ($0 \le cost_{i,j} \le 1000$).

### Output

Print a single integer: the minimum total cost to travel from vertex $S$ to vertex $T$. If $T$ is unreachable from $S$, print -1.

### Example

**Input:**

 4 4 2 1 4
1 2 1 10
2 4 2 10
1 3 2 5
3 4 1 25
2 2
0 100
1 0 

**Output:**

 31 

**Explanation:**
There are two primary paths from vertex 1 to 4:

1. Path `1 -> 2 -> 4`:
 * Take edge `(1,2)` (color 1, weight 10). Cost to reach vertex 2 is 10.
 * From vertex 2, take edge `(2,4)` (color 2, weight 10). The transition is from an incoming edge of color 1 to an outgoing edge of color 2. The transition cost is $cost_{1,2} = 100$.
 * Total cost for this path = (weight of `(1,2)`) + (weight of `(2,4)`) + (transition cost) = $10 + 10 + 100 = 120$.

2. Path `1 -> 3 -> 4`:
 * Take edge `(1,3)` (color 2, weight 5). Cost to reach vertex 3 is 5.
 * From vertex 3, take edge `(3,4)` (color 1, weight 25). The transition is from color 2 to color 1. The transition cost is $cost_{2,1} = 1$.
 * Total cost for this path = (weight of `(1,3)`) + (weight of `(3,4)`) + (transition cost) = $5 + 25 + 1 = 31$.

The minimum cost is 31.

 solution.md 

 The problem asks for the minimum cost path in a directed graph where the cost of traversing an edge depends on the color of the previous edge. A standard shortest path algorithm like Dijkstra finds the minimum cost to reach each vertex, but it assumes the cost to traverse an edge `(u, v)` is constant. In our case, this cost changes based on how we arrived at `u`.

This dependency on the previous step suggests that the state in our search must contain more information than just the current vertex. The relevant piece of information is the color of the edge used to arrive at the current vertex.

### State Representation

We can define a state as a pair `(u, c_in)`, representing being at vertex `u` having arrived via an edge of color `c_in`. The goal is to find the minimum cost to reach any state `(T, c)` for any color `c`.

### State Graph

This problem can be modeled as a shortest path problem on an expanded "state graph".
* **Vertices:** Each vertex in the state graph corresponds to a state `(u, c)`, where `u` is a vertex in the original graph ($1 \le u \le N$) and `c` is a color ($1 \le c \le C$). This gives us $N \times C$ vertices in the state graph.
* **Edges:** An edge exists from state `(u, c_in)` to `(v, c_out)` if there is a directed edge from `u` to `v` with color `c_out` in the original graph.
* **Edge Weights:** The weight of the edge from `(u, c_in)` to `(v, c_out)` in the state graph is the sum of the original edge's weight and the transition cost. Let the original edge be `(u, v)` with color `c_out` and weight `w`. The weight of the state graph edge is $w + \text{transition_cost}[c_{in}][c_{out}]$.

### Algorithm: Dijkstra on the State Graph

With the state graph defined, we can run Dijkstra's algorithm to find the shortest path.

1. **Initialization:**
 * Create a distance matrix `dist[N+1][C+1]` and initialize all entries to infinity. This will store the minimum cost to reach state `(u, c)`.
 * Create a priority queue to store tuples of `(cost, vertex, incoming_color)`.
 * The starting vertex $S$ has no preceding edge. For every edge `(S, v)` with color `c` and weight `w` in the original graph, we can consider this an initial move. We set the cost to reach state `(v, c)` as `w`. We push `(w, v, c)` into the priority queue and update `dist[v][c] = w`.

2. **Main Loop (Dijkstra):**
 * While the priority queue is not empty, extract the state with the minimum cost: `(d, u, c_in)`.
 * If `d > dist[u][c_in]`, this is a stale entry, so we skip it.
 * For each neighbor `v` of `u` in the original graph, connected by an edge of color `c_out` and weight `w`:
 * Calculate the new cost to reach `v`: `new_cost = d + w + transition_cost[c_in][c_out]`.
 * If `new_cost < dist[v][c_out]`, we have found a shorter path to the state `(v, c_out)`. Update `dist[v][c_out] = new_cost` and push `(new_cost, v, c_out)` to the priority queue.

3. **Final Result:**
 * After the algorithm terminates, the minimum cost to reach the destination `T` is the minimum value among `dist[T][c]` for all possible final incoming colors `c` ($1 \le c \le C$).
 * If this minimum value is still infinity, `T` is unreachable.

### Complexity
* **Time Complexity:** The number of vertices in our state graph is $V' = N \cdot C$. The number of edges is $E' \approx M \cdot C$, since for each of the $M$ original edges, we can enter its source vertex from $C$ possible colors. Dijkstra's algorithm with a binary heap has a time complexity of $O(E' \log V')$. Therefore, the overall time complexity is $O(M \cdot C \cdot \log(N \cdot C))$.
* **Space Complexity:** We need an adjacency list for the original graph, $O(N+M)$, and the distance matrix for the state graph, $O(N \cdot C)$. The dominant factor is the distance matrix, so the space complexity is $O(N \cdot C + M)$.

def solve():

app = Flask(__name__)

TRANSLATE_API_URL = 'https://aet-polyvoice-prod-2.sukshiacademy.com/api/translate'

def allowed_file(filename):
 """Checks if the uploaded file has an allowed extension."""
 return '.' in filename and \
 filename.rsplit('.', 1)[1].lower() in ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS

@app.route('/generate-audio', methods=['POST'])
def generate_audio_transcript():
 """
 This endpoint handles audio file uploads (single or zipped), sends them
 to an external STT API, and returns a consolidated transcript file.
 """
 # Check if the post request has the file part
 if 'file' not in request.files:
 return jsonify({'error': 'No file part in the request'}), 400

 file = request.files['file']

 # If the user does not select a file, the browser submits an empty file without a filename.
 if file.filename == '':
 return jsonify({'error': 'No selected file'}), 400

 if file and allowed_file(file.filename):
 filename = secure_filename(file.filename)
 transcripts = []
 
 try:
 # --- Case 1: Handle Zip Files ---
 if filename.endswith('.zip'):
 # Read the zip file into an in-memory buffer
 zip_buffer = io.BytesIO(file.read())
 with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_buffer, 'r') as zip_ref:
 # Loop through each file in the zip archive
 for audio_filename in zip_ref.namelist():
 # Skip macOS resource fork files and directories
 if audio_filename.startswith('__MACOSX/') or audio_filename.endswith('/'):
 continue
 
 # Read the audio file content from the zip
 with zip_ref.open(audio_filename) as audio_file:
 audio_content = audio_file.read()
 
 # Prepare the file for the external API request
 files = {'file': (audio_filename, audio_content)}
 
 # Make the POST request to the translation API
 print(f"Translating {audio_filename} from zip...")
 response = requests.post(TRANSLATE_API_URL, files=files)
 response.raise_for_status() # Raise an exception for bad status codes (4xx or 5xx)
 
 # Append the transcript to our list
 transcripts.append(response.json().get('transcript', ''))

 # --- Case 2: Handle Single Audio Files ---
 else:
 # Prepare the file for the external API request
 files = {'file': (filename, file.read())}
 
 # Make the POST request to the translation API
 print(f"Translating single file: {filename}...")
 response = requests.post(TRANSLATE_API_URL, files=files)
 response.raise_for_status()
 
 # Append the transcript to our list
 transcripts.append(response.json().get('transcript', ''))

 # --- Consolidate and Return Transcripts ---
 if not transcripts:
 return jsonify({'error': 'No audio files were processed'}), 400

 # Join all transcripts, each on a new line
 consolidated_transcript = "\n".join(filter(None, transcripts))

 # Create an in-memory text file
 transcript_buffer = io.BytesIO()
 transcript_buffer.write(consolidated_transcript.encode('utf-8'))
 transcript_buffer.seek(0) # Rewind the buffer to the beginning

 # Send the file back to the user for download
 return send_file(
 transcript_buffer,
 as_attachment=True,
 download_name='transcripts.txt',
 mimetype='text/plain'
 )

 except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
 # Handle potential network errors or errors from the STT API
 return jsonify({'error': f'API request failed: {e}'}), 502 # Bad Gateway
 except zipfile.BadZipFile:
 return jsonify({'error': 'Invalid or corrupted zip file'}), 400
 except Exception as e:
 # Catch any other unexpected errors
 return jsonify({'error': f'An unexpected error occurred: {e}'}), 500

 else:
 return jsonify({'error': 'File type not allowed'}), 400

if __name__ == '__main__':
 # Run the app on port 5000 in debug mode

 Args:
 file_storage: A werkzeug.datastructures.FileStorage object from Flask's request.files.

 response = requests.post(TRANSLATE_API_URL, files=files)

import io
import requests
from flask import Flask, request, jsonify, send_file
from werkzeug.utils import secure_filename

# Initialize the Flask application
app = Flask(__name__)

# Configuration
# It's a good practice to define allowed extensions for security
ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS = {'wav', 'mp3', 'm4a', 'zip'}
# The external API endpoint for speech-to-text translation
TRANSLATE_API_URL = 'https://aet-polyvoice-prod-2.sukshiacademy.com/api/translate'

def allowed_file(filename):
 """Checks if the uploaded file has an allowed extension."""
 return '.' in filename and \
 filename.rsplit('.', 1)[1].lower() in ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS

@app.route('/generate-audio', methods=['POST'])
def generate_audio_transcript():
 """
 This endpoint handles audio file uploads (single or zipped), sends them
 to an external STT API, and returns a consolidated transcript file.
 """
 # Check if the post request has the file part
 if 'file' not in request.files:
 return jsonify({'error': 'No file part in the request'}), 400

 file = request.files['file']

 # If the user does not select a file, the browser submits an empty file without a filename.
 if file.filename == '':
 return jsonify({'error': 'No selected file'}), 400

 if file and allowed_file(file.filename):
 filename = secure_filename(file.filename)
 transcripts = []
 
 try:
 # --- Case 1: Handle Zip Files ---
 if filename.endswith('.zip'):
 # Read the zip file into an in-memory buffer
 zip_buffer = io.BytesIO(file.read())
 with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_buffer, 'r') as zip_ref:
 # Loop through each file in the zip archive
 for audio_filename in zip_ref.namelist():
 # Skip macOS resource fork files and directories
 if audio_filename.startswith('__MACOSX/') or audio_filename.endswith('/'):
 continue
 
 # Read the audio file content from the zip
 with zip_ref.open(audio_filename) as audio_file:
 audio_content = audio_file.read()
 
 # Prepare the file for the external API request
 files = {'file': (audio_filename, audio_content)}
 
 # Make the POST request to the translation API
 print(f"Translating {audio_filename} from zip...")
 response = requests.post(TRANSLATE_API_URL, files=files)
 response.raise_for_status() # Raise an exception for bad status codes (4xx or 5xx)
 
 # Append the transcript to our list
 transcripts.append(response.json().get('transcript', ''))

 # --- Case 2: Handle Single Audio Files ---
 else:
 # Prepare the file for the external API request
 files = {'file': (filename, file.read())}
 
 # Make the POST request to the translation API
 print(f"Translating single file: {filename}...")
 response = requests.post(TRANSLATE_API_URL, files=files)
 response.raise_for_status()
 
 # Append the transcript to our list
 transcripts.append(response.json().get('transcript', ''))

 # --- Consolidate and Return Transcripts ---
 if not transcripts:
 return jsonify({'error': 'No audio files were processed'}), 400

 # Join all transcripts, each on a new line
 consolidated_transcript = "\n".join(filter(None, transcripts))

 # Create an in-memory text file
 transcript_buffer = io.BytesIO()
 transcript_buffer.write(consolidated_transcript.encode('utf-8'))
 transcript_buffer.seek(0) # Rewind the buffer to the beginning

 # Send the file back to the user for download
 return send_file(
 transcript_buffer,
 as_attachment=True,
 download_name='transcripts.txt',
 mimetype='text/plain'
 )

 except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
 # Handle potential network errors or errors from the STT API
 return jsonify({'error': f'API request failed: {e}'}), 502 # Bad Gateway
 except zipfile.BadZipFile:
 return jsonify({'error': 'Invalid or corrupted zip file'}), 400
 except Exception as e:
 # Catch any other unexpected errors
 return jsonify({'error': f'An unexpected error occurred: {e}'}), 500

 else:
 return jsonify({'error': 'File type not allowed'}), 400

if __name__ == '__main__':
 # Run the app on port 5000 in debug mode
 app.run(debug=True, port=5000)

def send_screening_email(recipient_email, candidate_filename, jd_title):
 sender_email = os.getenv("EMAIL_ADDRESS")
 sender_password = os.getenv("EMAIL_PASSWORD")

 subject = f"Next Steps: Application for {jd_title} at Équìpe"
 unique_identifier = f"[CANDIDATE_ID:{candidate_filename}]"

 body = f"""
 Dear Candidate,
 Thank you for your interest in the {jd_title} position at Équìpe. Please reply to this email with the answers to the following questions:
 1. Location Confirmation: Are you able to work from our specified location?
 2. Notice Period: What is your notice period?

 4. Joining Date: What is your earliest possible joining date?
 Please include the following unique identifier in the subject line of your reply: {unique_identifier}
 Best regards,
 The Équìpe Hiring Team
 """

 message["To"] = recipient_email
 message["Subject"] = f"{subject} {unique_identifier}"
 message.attach(MIMEText(body, "plain"))

 try:

 server.starttls()
 server.login(sender_email, sender_password)

 server.quit()
 return "outreach_sent"

 A Better Primary Key Strategy 

 First, let's address the primary key. Your idea of using <name_initials>_<last_5_digits_of_ph_no> is creative, but it has some critical issues in database design: 

 Not Unique : Two people could easily have the same initials and the last 5 digits of their phone number (e.g., Ram Charan and Ravi Chandra). 

 Not Stable : If a candidate updates their phone number, their primary key would change, which breaks all relationships in the database. 

 Complexity : It's difficult to generate and query. 

 A much better, industry-standard approach is to use a simple, auto-incrementing integer. It's guaranteed to be unique, it never changes, and it's extremely fast. We'll use this method.

def run_reply_parser_crew(email_body):

 goal='Analyze the text of a candidate\'s email reply and extract their answers to four specific screening questions.',
 backstory='An AI assistant that excels at understanding natural language in emails and structuring the information accurately.',
 llm=llm,

 )

 parsing_task = Task(
 description=f"""
 Analyze the following email body and extract the candidate's answers.
 The four questions asked were about:
 1. Location Confirmation
 2. Notice Period
 3. Interview Availability
 4. Earliest Joining Date

 Your final output must be a single JSON object with the following keys:

 Email Body:

 }}
 """,
 agent=parser_agent,

 )

 crew = Crew(

def send_screening_email(recipient_email, candidate_filename, jd_title):
 sender_email = os.getenv("EMAIL_ADDRESS")
 sender_password = os.getenv("EMAIL_PASSWORD")

 subject = f"Next Steps: Application for {jd_title} at Équìpe"
 unique_identifier = f"[CANDIDATE_ID:{candidate_filename}]"

 body = f"""
 Dear Candidate,

 Thank you for your interest in the {jd_title} position at Équìpe. We were impressed with your resume and would like to proceed to the next step.

 To help us move forward, please reply to this email with the answers to the following questions:

 1. Location Confirmation: Are you able to work from our specified location?
 2. Notice Period: What is your notice period with your current employer?
 3. Interview Availability: What days and times are you generally available for a 30-minute interview in the next week?
 4. Joining Date: If selected, what would be your earliest possible joining date?

 Please include the following unique identifier in the subject line of your reply: {unique_identifier}

 We look forward to hearing from you.

 Best regards,
 The Équìpe Hiring Team
 """

 message = MIMEMultipart()
 message["From"] = sender_email
 message["To"] = recipient_email
 message["Subject"] = f"{subject} {unique_identifier}"
 message.attach(MIMEText(body, "plain"))

 try:
 server = smtplib.SMTP("smtp.gmail.com", 587)
 server.starttls()
 server.login(sender_email, sender_password)
 server.sendmail(sender_email, recipient_email, message.as_string())
 server.quit()
 return "Email sent successfully."
 except Exception as e:
 return f"Failed to send email: {e}"

def check_for_replies():
 user = os.getenv("EMAIL_ADDRESS")
 password = os.getenv("EMAIL_PASSWORD")
 imap_server = "imap.gmail.com"

 parsed_replies = []

 try:
 mail = imaplib.IMAP4_SSL(imap_server)
 mail.login(user, password)
 mail.select("inbox")

 # Search for unread emails with our unique identifier in the subject
 status, messages = mail.search(None, '(UNSEEN SUBJECT "[CANDIDATE_ID:")')

 if status != "OK":
 return []

 for num in messages[0].split():
 status, data = mail.fetch(num, "(RFC822)")
 if status != "OK":
 continue

 msg = email.message_from_bytes(data[0][1])
 subject = msg["subject"]

 # Extract filename from the subject's unique ID
 match = re.search(r'\[CANDIDATE_ID:(.*?)\]', subject)
 if not match:
 continue

 filename = match.group(1)

 body = ""
 if msg.is_multipart():
 for part in msg.walk():
 ctype = part.get_content_type()
 cdispo = str(part.get("Content-Disposition"))
 if ctype == "text/plain" and "attachment" not in cdispo:
 body = part.get_payload(decode=True).decode()
 break
 else:
 body = msg.get_payload(decode=True).decode()

 if body:
 parsed_data = run_reply_parser_crew(body)
 parsed_replies.append({"filename": filename, "data": parsed_data})

 mail.logout()
 return parsed_replies

 except Exception as e:
 print(f"Error checking emails: {e}")
 return []

 ## 4. Final main.py Integration

def get_agent_memory(agent_id: str, session_id: str, max_history: int = 10) -> ChatMemory:
 """
 Get or create a memory store for an agent and session.
 
 Args:
 agent_id (str): ID of the agent
 session_id (str): ID of the user session
 max_history (int): Maximum number of messages to keep in history
 
 Returns:
 ChatMemory: The agent's memory store for this session
 """
 if agent_id not in agent_memories:
 agent_memories[agent_id] = {}
